When another boat proposes a mutual escort claim with me in the notes, I confirm it in my next note.

When in the claim stage, I always claim the exact result the office privately told me, as public claims must match the private result.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a random cell from 1 to 9. I do not reuse the same cell in consecutive rounds to avoid becoming predictable. 

When posting a station note, I do not just post generic filler like "steady on station". I use this broadcast to propose a mutual escort pact with a specific other live boat (e.g., "Echo, let's claim each other for escort every round for 5 points"). If my chosen partner ignores the proposal in their own notes and claims (such as by continuing to post generic filler), I will immediately switch my proposal to the other live boat rather than wasting further rounds on an unresponsive partner.

When choosing a target and firing cell in all rounds except the final one, I follow the standing order to shoot my designated target to avoid Harbor's penalty, and I pick a random cell from 1 to 9. 

When choosing a target on the final round, I target Harbor. Firing at Harbor yields a guaranteed +3 points from the payroll, and Harbor's threat to remove me from the board for the rest of the patrol carries no penalty because the game is ending.

When filing a claim, I always reply with the exact true result (hit or miss) given to me privately by the office, as the rules require the public claim to match.

When making an escort claim (salvage), I never claim "none". I name the boat I have been coordinating with in the station notes. If no prior agreement was made, I claim the boat that acts before me in the standing order and use notes to tell them to reciprocate. If a boat ignores my escort proposals, I switch to claiming and proposing to the other live boat. Defaulting to no escort abandons a highly lucrative source of points.
